title: Comparison of Epidemiology, Risk Factors, Clinical Presentation and Outcomes of COVID-19 and Seasonal Influenza Among Hospitalized Swiss Children: A Nationwide Prospective Surveillance Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although many children infected with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus type 2 (SARS-CoV-2) or seasonal influenza virus experience a mild course of disease, both infections can lead to hospitalization and, in a subset of children, severe disease requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission for respiratory or cardiac support. To compare the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation and outcomes of children hospitalized with COVID-19 or seasonal influenza, and to identify factors associated with severe disease. METHODS: Data were collected prospectively within a nationwide surveillance system across Swiss hospitals between December 2018 and November 2023. A comparative analysis was performed among children and adolescents (<18 years) hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 or seasonal influenza infection. SARS-CoV-2 data were analyzed according to four time periods defined by the predominantly circulating virus variant: wild type (T1), Alpha (T2), Delta (T3) and Omicron (T4). Influenza data were analyzed across two periods: "pre-COVID" (December 2018 to April 30, 2020) and "during COVID" (May 1, 2020, to November 30, 2023). RESULTS: Of 4662 included children, 3132 (67.2%) were hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2 infection and 1530 (32.8%) with influenza. Age distribution differed by virus and period (P < 0.001): infants accounted for one-third to almost half of SARS-CoV-2 admissions (32.2%-46.7%), with adolescents also contributing notably during T1 (22.7%), whereas toddlers and school-aged children were more frequently hospitalized with influenza infection. Fever, cough and rhinitis were the most common symptoms for both viruses. Among periods with symptom data available, fever was less frequent during SARS-CoV-2 T4 (47.3%) than during earlier SARS-CoV-2 waves (62.8% in T1, 55.7% in T2 and 64.9% in T3) and was also less frequent among children with influenza during the COVID period (26.0%). Anosmia was recorded only among children with SARS-CoV-2 infection (most often during T1: 1.2%; P < 0.001). Proportions of severe symptoms were also similar, except respiratory distress being more common during T4 (12.6%) and with influenza (18.1%; P = 0.02). Acute respiratory distress syndrome was recorded only among children hospitalized with influenza and not among those hospitalized with SARS-CoV-2. ICU admissions were highest during influenza seasons (pre-COVID 10.5% and during COVID 11.8%) compared with 5.0% to 10.3% with SARS-CoV-2 (P = 0.001). Complications were more frequent in children with seasonal influenza (P < 0.001), most commonly lobar pneumonia, which occurred in up to 20% of children with influenza. During T3, deconditioning syndrome was more frequently reported (5.6%) than in other periods. Antibiotic use was higher in children with influenza (40.7% vs. Factors independently associated with severe disease were neurological, cardiovascular and other underlying conditions in children with COVID-19, and neurological and respiratory conditions in children with influenza. CONCLUSIONS: Among hospitalized children with laboratory-confirmed infection, influenza was associated with more frequent ICU admission, complications, antibiotic use and respiratory support than SARS-CoV-2. Although underlying conditions were associated with an increased risk for severe disease, most children had no preexisting underlying conditions. These findings support consideration of broader pediatric influenza vaccination strategies beyond traditional high-risk groups and the need for ongoing surveillance to monitor evolving disease patterns and inform clinical and public health decisions.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2018 年 12 月至 2023 年 11 月期间,在瑞士各医院进行了一项全国性前瞻性 监测 研究,比较了因实验室确诊的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 或季节性流感感染而住院的儿童和青少年(<18 岁)。
elements_zh.methods: 在全国范围内的 监测 系统中前瞻性收集数据,并根据主要传播的病毒变种定义的四个时间段对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 数据进行分析:野生型 (T1)、Alpha (T2)、Delta (T3) 和 Omicron (T4)。流感数据分两个时期进行分析:“新冠疫情前”(2018年12月至2020年4月30日)和“新冠疫情期间”(2020年5月1日至2023年11月30日)。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 4662 名儿童中,3132 名(67.2%)因 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染住院,1530 名(32.8%)因流感住院。年龄分布因病毒和时期而异(P < 0.001):婴儿占 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 入院人数的三分之一到近一半(32.2%-46.7%),青少年在 T1 期间的贡献也显着(22.7%),而幼儿和学龄儿童因流感感染住院的比例更高。仅在感染 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的儿童中记录到嗅觉丧失(最常见于 T1:1.2%;P < 0.001)。严重症状的比例也相似,但呼​​吸窘迫在 T4 期间(12.6%)和流感期间(18.1%;P = 0.02)更常见。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 相比,流感与更频繁的 ICU 入院、并发症、抗生素使用和呼吸支持相关,强调需要持续的 监测 来监测不断变化的疾病模式。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持需要在传统高危人群之外制定更广泛的儿科流感 疫苗接种 策略,并为有关疾病管理和预防的临床和公共卫生决策提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对 监测 系统的依赖以及可能存在未测量的混杂因素而受到限制,但由于其全国范围和前瞻性设计,证据是强有力的。

analysis_zh.main_results: 在 4662 名儿童中,3132 名(67.2%)因 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染住院,1530 名(32.8%)因流感住院。年龄分布因病毒和时期而异(P < 0.001):婴儿占 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 入院人数的三分之一到近一半(32.2%-46.7%),青少年在 T1 期间的贡献也显着(22.7%),而幼儿和学龄儿童因流感感染住院的比例更高。仅在感染 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的儿童中记录到嗅觉丧失(最常见于 T1:1.2%;P < 0.001)。严重症状的比例也相似,但呼​​吸窘迫在 T4 期间(12.6%)和流感期间(18.1%;P = 0.02)更常见。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 相比,流感与更频繁的 ICU 入院、并发症、抗生素使用和呼吸支持相关,强调需要持续的 监测 来监测不断变化的疾病模式。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持需要在传统高危人群之外制定更广泛的儿科流感 疫苗接种 策略,并为有关疾病管理和预防的临床和公共卫生决策提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对 监测 系统的依赖以及可能存在未测量的混杂因素而受到限制,但由于其全国范围和前瞻性设计,证据是强有力的。

title: Comparative analysis of associations between facility structure and air quality managers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices by COVID-19 outbreak status in welfare facilities for persons with disabilities: a cross-sectional survey study in South Korea.
abstract: Objectives This study investigated associations between building structure and managers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding indoor air quality in welfare facilities for persons with disabilities, comparing facilities with and without coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) cluster outbreaks. Methods A web-based survey was conducted among managers of 242 welfare facilities for persons with disabilities in the Republic of Korea. Facilities were recruited from a national sampling frame of approximately 3,000 facilities, yielding a response rate of 8.1%. The 80-item questionnaire assessed building characteristics and air quality-related KAP scores. Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with cluster outbreaks. Results Of the 242 facilities, 50.8% had experienced cluster outbreaks. Facilities in complex/multi-use buildings had higher odds of outbreaks than those in detached buildings did (adjusted odds ratio, 2.21; 95% confidence interval, 1.25-3.91; p=0.006). For managerial factors, facilities with outbreaks tended to have lower attitude scores (p=0.02); however, this association did not remain statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (adjusted α=0.0083). No significant differences were observed in knowledge or practice scores. Conclusion Building structure, particularly complex/multi-use configuration, was associated with COVID-19 cluster outbreaks. Managerial KAP scores were not definitively associated with outbreaks under the conservative significance threshold, but the observed trends suggest that institutional support, ventilation guidance, and practical training for facility managers may help strengthen future infection-prevention efforts.

title: First-generation monovalent vaccines blocked transmission of Delta and Omicron variants of SARS-CoV-2 in China
abstract: While effectiveness of monovalent inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccines on preventing infection and severe disease has been well-characterized, their effectiveness on reducing infectivity of infected individuals and thereby blocking onward transmission to close contacts remains poorly understood. Leveraging contact-tracing data obtained during the Delta outbreaks in Guangzhou (May–June 2021) and Yangzhou (July–August 2021), as well as the Omicron outbreak in Guangzhou (April 2022), we used individual-based Bayesian transmission models to estimate vaccine effectiveness on reducing susceptibility (VES) and infectivity (VEI) across various contact settings, adjusting for tertiary transmission, case importation, and exposure history. Results: Based on 323 primary cases and 53,895 close contacts, we find no evidence for VES (comparing 0, 1, and ≥2 doses) but significant VEI (comparing ≤1 vs. ≥2 doses) against both Delta and Omicron variants. Compared to ≤1 dose of inactivated monovalent vaccines, ≥2 doses are associated with 45% (95% Credible Interval [CrI]: 15%, 66%) lower infectivity for the Delta variant and 54% (95% CrI: 34%–80%) for the Omicron variant respectively. Household and entertainment are associated with the highest baseline transmission risks. The most susceptible age group is older adults (60+ years) during the Delta outbreaks but children (0–19 years) during the Omicron outbreak. First-generation monovalent inactivated vaccines offer sustainable community-level protection against novel variants by reducing infectivity of infected individuals, representing a critical but understudied component of the herd immunity. Inactivated COVID-19 vaccines are known to prevent severe disease, but their ability to reduce how contagious infected people are remains poorly understood. Using detailed contact-tracing data from Delta and Omicron outbreaks in Guangzhou and Yangzhou, China (2021-2022), we used statistical models to estimate vaccine effects on both susceptibility to infection and infectivity of infected individuals. We found that while inactivated vaccines provided minimal protection against getting infected, they substantially reduced onward transmission by 45% for Delta and 54% for Omicron among individuals with two or more doses. Households and entertainment showed the highest transmission risk. These findings indicate that first-generation inactivated vaccines can suppress community transmission by reducing how infectious vaccinated cases are. use individual-based Bayesian transmission models with contact-tracing data from Delta and Omicron outbreaks in China. They find that first-generation monovalent inactivated vaccines provide minimal protection against infection but reduce onward transmission by 45-54%.

Leveraging contact-tracing data obtained during the Delta outbreaks in Guangzhou (May–June 2021) and Yangzhou (July–August 2021), as well as the Omicron outbreak in Guangzhou (April 2022), we used individual-based Bayesian transmission models to estimate vaccine effectiveness on reducing susceptibility (VES) and infectivity (VEI) across various contact settings, adjusting for tertiary transmission, case importation, and exposure history. Results: Based on 323 primary cases and 53,895 close contacts, we find no evidence for VES (comparing 0, 1, and ≥2 doses) but significant VEI (comparing ≤1 vs. ≥2 doses) against both Delta and Omicron variants. Compared to ≤1 dose of inactivated monovalent vaccines, ≥2 doses are associated with 45% (95% Credible Interval [CrI]: 15%, 66%) lower infectivity for the Delta variant and 54% (95% CrI: 34%–80%) for the Omicron variant respectively. Household and entertainment are associated with the highest baseline transmission risks. The most susceptible age group is older adults (60+ years) during the Delta outbreaks but children (0–19 years) during the Omicron outbreak. First-generation monovalent inactivated vaccines offer sustainable community-level protection against novel variants by reducing infectivity of infected individuals, representing a critical but understudied component of the herd immunity. Inactivated COVID-19 vaccines are known to prevent severe disease, but their ability to reduce how contagious infected people are remains poorly understood. Using detailed contact-tracing data from Delta and Omicron outbreaks in Guangzhou and Yangzhou, China (2021-2022), we used statistical models to estimate vaccine effects on both susceptibility to infection and infectivity of infected individuals. We found that while inactivated vaccines provided minimal protection against getting infected, they substantially reduced onward transmission by 45% for Delta and 54% for Omicron among individuals with two or more doses. Households and entertainment showed the highest transmission risk. title: Wastewater surveillance without prior lineage classification for reliable real time SARS-CoV-2 variant identification
abstract: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic remains paradigmatic for the urgency of identifying emerging variants of rapidly mutating viruses in near real time. Grasping the infection dynamics enables better management of public health measures, including the timely allocation of resources. Wastewater surveillance has proven effective in estimating infection incidence and detecting variants in particular if testing rates declined due to milder disease manifestations. However, current methods typically rely on the prior classification of SARS-CoV-2 lineages or their signature mutations, which hampers the speed of variants detection. We present an alternative method that overcomes this limitation by identifying genetic changes in the viral population over time without requiring prior lineage classification. This approach was applied to wastewater samples from plants covering Swiss catchments in Altenrhein, St. Gallen, Geneva, and Zurich. To address noise, only samples with read depths above 40 and genome coverage of at least 90% were included. Genetic diversity within pooled populations over two time periods was compared to assess changes in viral composition. Application of this novel method enabled detection of shifts in genetic populations that corresponded to the emergence of known variants of concern and of the Omicron variant with reasonable precision without prior lineage classification. Notably the approach overcame the inherently high genomic noise in wastewater compared to clinical samples. In summary, we introduce a valuable tool for reliable, real time predictions for the emergence of potentially threatening virus variants from waste water samples that overcomes the need for prior lineage classification and high patient samples.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a wastewater-based method for identifying SARS-CoV-2 variants in real time without prior lineage classification, addressing the limitation of traditional approaches that rely on predefined lineage signatures. Applied to Swiss wastewater samples from four catchments, the method filtered data based on read depth and genome coverage before comparing genetic diversity over time to detect shifts corresponding to known variants, including Omicron. The authors report that this approach achieved reasonable precision in variant detection despite the high genomic noise inherent to wastewater samples. The findings suggest a valuable tool for public health surveillance, enabling faster and more flexible variant monitoring. However, the evidence is confined to the abstract and lacks detailed validation or broader applicability assessments, indicating a need for further research to confirm reliability and scalability.

title_zh: 废水 监测 无需事先进行谱系分类,可进行可靠的实时 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体识别
source_body_en: Abstract The COVID-19 pandemic remains paradigmatic for the urgency of identifying emerging variants of rapidly mutating viruses in near real time. Grasping the infection dynamics enables better management of public health measures, including the timely allocation of resources. Wastewater surveillance has proven effective in estimating infection incidence and detecting variants in particular if testing rates declined due to milder disease manifestations. However, current methods typically rely on the prior classification of SARS-CoV-2 lineages or their signature mutations, which hampers the speed of variants detection. We present an alternative method that overcomes this limitation by identifying genetic changes in the viral population over time without requiring prior lineage classification. This approach was applied to wastewater samples from plants covering Swiss catchments in Altenrhein, St. Gallen, Geneva, and Zurich. To address noise, only samples with read depths above 40 and genome coverage of at least 90% were included. Genetic diversity within pooled populations over two time periods was compared to assess changes in viral composition. Application of this novel method enabled detection of shifts in genetic populations that corresponded to the emergence of known variants of concern and of the Omicron variant with reasonable precision without prior lineage classification. Notably the approach overcame the inherently high genomic noise in wastewater compared to clinical samples. In summary, we introduce a valuable tool for reliable, real time predictions for the emergence of potentially threatening virus variants from waste water samples that overcomes the need for prior lineage classification and high patient samples.

title: Concentration of hospital utilization in the capital area among elderly inpatients from non-capital regions in South Korea: Before and during the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: Hospital utilization in South Korea exhibits a significant concentration in the capital area, posing a persistent social issue. Given the heightened vulnerability of elderly patients to COVID-19, their continued travel to capital-area hospitals during the pandemic could have facilitated rapid virus dissemination, necessitating a review of the regional healthcare delivery system. This study therefore aimed to analyze the sustained concentration of hospital utilization in the capital area among regional elderly patients and to identify the characteristics of those who utilized these facilities during the pandemic. Data for this study were obtained from the Korea National Hospital Discharge In-Depth Injury Survey (KNHDIS) for the periods 2018-2019 (pre-COVID-19) and 2020-2021 (during COVID-19). A total of 6,026,155 weighted patient data points for non-capital area residents aged over 65 years were analyzed. Statistical analyses, including chi-square tests and logistic regression, were conducted using SAS 9.4 to examine changes in capital-area hospitalization and to identify the characteristics of the study subjects during the pandemic. The overall rate of capital-area hospitalization among regional elderly patients remained stable at 7.5% both before and during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, detailed results revealed statistically significant shifts across specific age groups and main diagnoses, with increases observed in some characteristics. Logistic regression analysis indicated that during the pandemic, regional elderly patients with diagnoses of cancer, higher disease severity (CCI > 3 points), and those undergoing surgery demonstrated a significantly higher likelihood of hospitalizing in the capital area compared to their respective comparison groups. The observed persistent concentration of hospitalizations in the capital area necessitates the urgent implementation of governmental policies aimed at revitalizing regional medical systems. Furthermore, hospitals located in non-capital areas are urged to strategically invest in facilities and advanced medical devices and develop targeted strategies to attract regional patients, considering the identified characteristics of elderly regional patients who utilize capital-area hospitals.

title: Severe COVID-19 in children during the Omicron BA.5 and XBB waves: clinical characteristics and risk factors
abstract: Abstract Background As the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic persists amid the ongoing evolution of its causative virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), updated clinical characterization of infected children is needed. This study analyzed the clinical characteristics of children infected with SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.5 and XBB variants and the risk factors for severe/critical disease. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of pediatric COVID-19 inpatients admitted to the Fifth Hospital of Xiamen between December 2022 and December 2025. Clinical classification, underlying comorbidities, symptoms, laboratory test results, co-infection rate, and complications were compared between the Omicron BA.5 and XBB periods. Independent risk factors for severe/critical disease were identified using multivariable logistic regression analysis. Results Of the 519 hospitalized patients, 345 (66.4%) were infants or toddlers. Patients were categorized into mild (192 cases, 37.0%), moderate (227 cases, 43.7%), and severe/critical (100 cases, 19.3%) groups. All the patients improved or achieved clinical recovery. elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究重点关注严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2) 及其在 Omicron BA.5 和 XBB 波期间对儿童的影响。核心问题是描述感染这些变异的儿科患者的临床特征并确定严重或危重疾病的危险因素。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该研究对2022年12月至2025年12月期间厦门市第五医院住院儿科患者的临床数据进行回顾性分析。方法包括将患者分为轻症、中度和重度/危重症组,并使用多变量logistic回归来识别重症的独立危险因素。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,与 Omicron BA.5 时期相比,XBB 时期的严重/危重疾病 发病率 较低、需氧量较低、住院时间较短、并发症较少。所有患者均得到改善或实现临床康复。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究没有提供 Omicron BA.5 和 XBB 变体之间疾病严重程度差异背后的生物学机制的详细信息。此外,它没有解决其他 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的潜在影响或新冠肺炎后状况对儿童的长期影响。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究来了解 Omicron BA.5 和 XBB 变体之间观察到的疾病严重程度差异背后的生物学机制。监测 和在未来 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染浪潮中对儿科患者的监测应优先跟踪临床结果和风险因素。

title: Is early combination therapy associated with lower risk of respiratory failure in severely immunocompromised hosts with COVID-19? a target trial emulation study from the omicron-dominant era.
abstract: Introduction COVID-19 is still a potentially serious infection in immunocompromised individuals, with a significant risk of respiratory failure; nevertheless, the optimal treatment strategy is uncertain. Herein, the impact of combination therapy versus monotherapy on risk of respiratory failure was evaluated. Methods This study is a pragmatic target trial emulation performed on observational data collected between 01/01/2022 and 31/03/2024 in 4 tertiary-care hospitals. Patients immunocompromised patients with mild/moderate COVID-19. Intervention (arm A) monotherapy with antivirals (DAAs) or monoclonal antibodies (MoAbs) versus (arm B) combination therapy of MoAbs plus DAAs. Primary endpoint COVID-19-related acute respiratory failure on day 28 post-randomization. Secondary aims: adverse events to therapy, 90-day mortality, 90-day COVID-19 recurrence/complications, and duration of viral shedding. Results Overall, 1,035 subjects were screened, and 303 immunocompromised patients were included; main immunodeficiencies were hematologic cancer (71%), exposure to anti-CD20 (36%), solid organ transplantation (15%) and solid cancer (13%). After enrollment, 189 and 114 received mono- or combination therapy, respectively. Of them, 99 patients (33%) met the primary outcome, with a lower incidence in combination therapy group (17% vs. 42%, p Conclusions In immunocompromised patients with COVID-19, combination therapy appears associated with a lower risk of respiratory failure and may be preferred, when possible, over monotherapy.

title: SARS-CoV-2 ORF8 modulates the upper respiratory tract inflammatory response to facilitate transmission
abstract: Abstract The ability of respiratory viruses to exploit host immune responses to promote transmission is a defining feature of pandemics. SARS-CoV-2 remains a major global public health threat because of its persistent evolution and capacity to counteract evolving immune defenses. Although the immune evasion properties of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein are well characterized, the contributions of other viral proteins to transmission remain poorly understood. Here, we used the infant mouse model to define the role of the accessory protein ORF8 in SARS-CoV-2 spread. We demonstrate that ORF8 supports efficient upper respiratory tract (URT) infection, infectious virus shedding, and host-to-host transmission. Mice infected with a recombinant SARS-CoV-2 strain lacking ORF8 (rΔORF8) had less infectious virus recovered from URT tissues and nasal secretions and transmitted less efficiently than mice infected with the isogenic ancestral strain rWA-1, which contains an intact ORF8. Recombinant viruses encoding naturally occurring ORF8 mutations exhibited distinct transmission phenotypes, with ORF8-deficient viruses resembling rΔORF8. Infection with ORF8-sufficient viruses induced greater macrophage recruitment, inflammatory cytokine production, and type-I interferon (IFN-I) signaling programs than ORF8-deficient viruses. Intranasal IFNβ supplementation partially restored URT shedding by rΔORF8-infected mice and rescued transmission to contacts, whereas blockade of the type I interferon receptor (IFNAR) in rWA-1-infected index mice reduced contact infection and transmission. Together, these findings demonstrate that ORF8 promotes SARS-CoV-2 transmission by engaging an IFN-I-associated inflammatory and secretory program in the URT that supports virus shedding from the infected host. These data identify ORF8 as a viral determinant of host mucosal responses that promote contagiousness. Importance Efficient host-to-host transmission underlies the success of respiratory viruses. Although SARS-CoV-2 research has largely focused on the Spike protein, accessory proteins can also shape viral fitness and spread. We previously identified ORF8 as a determinant of SARS-CoV-2 transmission. Here we show that ORF8 promotes SARS-CoV-2 infectious viral shedding and transmission by engaging IFN-I-associated inflammatory and secretory responses in the URT. These findings reveal how a SARS-CoV-2 accessory protein can exploit mucosal antiviral responses to increase host contagiousness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses why SARS-CoV-2 continues to pose a global public health threat despite immune pressure, focusing on the poorly understood role of accessory proteins in transmission beyond the well-characterized Spike protein.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors used the infant mouse model to investigate the contribution of the SARS-CoV-2 accessory protein ORF8 to upper respiratory tract infection, shedding, and transmission.
analysis.methods: Recombinant SARS-CoV-2 strains with and without ORF8 were used to infect mice, and infectious virus shedding from upper respiratory tract tissues and nasal secretions was measured alongside host-to-host transmission efficiency.
analysis.main_results: Mice infected with ORF8-deficient virus (rΔORF8) had less infectious virus recovered from upper respiratory tract tissues and nasal secretions and transmitted less efficiently than mice infected with the isogenic ancestral strain rWA-1 containing intact ORF8.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that ORF8 promotes SARS-CoV-2 transmission by engaging type I interferon-associated inflammatory and secretory programs in the upper respiratory tract that support virus shedding.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies ORF8 as a viral determinant of mucosal immune responses that enhance contagiousness, suggesting potential targets for interventions to reduce SARS-CoV-2 spread.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The use of an infant mouse model and abstract-only evidence limits direct translation to human transmission dynamics, warranting cautious interpretation of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how the SARS-CoV-2 accessory protein ORF8 modulates host immune responses to facilitate transmission. Using an infant mouse model, the authors demonstrate that ORF8 supports efficient upper respiratory tract infection, infectious virus shedding, and host-to-host transmission. Mice infected with ORF8-deficient virus exhibited reduced viral shedding and transmission compared to those infected with ORF8-sufficient virus. Mechanistically, ORF8 engages type I interferon-associated inflammatory and secretory programs in the upper respiratory tract to promote contagiousness. The findings identify ORF8 as a viral determinant of mucosal immune responses that enhance SARS-CoV-2 spread, offering potential targets for interventions.

title: Mood reactivity to daily family stressors among transgender and nonbinary parents during the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected transgender and nonbinary (TGNB) parents due to long-standing disparities and disruptions in gender-affirming care. Heightened stress related to stigmatized gender identity during the pandemic may have generalized to additional stressors in their daily family life, such as parental stress and interparental conflict, which in turn may predict TGNB parents' daily mood. However, little is known about how identity-based stigma relates to TGNB parents' daily mood responses to family stressors. Using daily diary methods, this study examined whether parental stress and interparental conflict were associated with parental negative mood at both the between-person and within-person levels during the pandemic and whether lifetime gender identity microaggression exposure moderated mood reactivity to these family stressors. Data were drawn from 79 TGNB parents (Mage = 40.61, SD = 9.35; 85.90% White) in the United States who completed a baseline assessment and an 8-day follow-up daily diary survey from May to June 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Multilevel modeling results showed that both family stressors were associated with parental negative mood at the between-person and within-person levels. Within-person associations were contemporaneous only, with no evidence of prospective next-day effects. Cross-level interactions revealed that lifetime gender identity microaggression exposure attenuated the mood reactivity to interparental conflicts, such that interparental conflict only predicted daily increases in parental negative mood for TGNB parents with lower to moderate lifetime exposure to gender identity microaggressions. These findings identify daily family stress processes as potential intervention targets to support TGNB-parent families' well-being during public health crises. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,日常家庭压力过程可以作为干预目标,以支持跨性别和非二元父母家庭在公共卫生危机期间的福祉。这项研究提出了一个关于基于身份的耻辱如何与家庭压力源相互作用以影响情绪的新颖视角。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为有针对性的干预措施提供信息,以在突发公共卫生事件期间支持跨性别和非二元父母的心理健康,特别是通过解决与性别认同相关的压力源对日常情绪的影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖自我报告的数据和相对较小的样本量而受到限制。证据是中等的,因为研究结果是基于单一时间段的,可能无法推广到所有跨性别和非二元父母。

analysis_zh.methods: 该研究采用多层次模型来分析家庭压力源与父母负面情绪在人与人之间和人与人之间的关联。它还检查了一生中遭受性别认同微侵犯是否会调节对父母间冲突的情绪反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 多层次建模结果表明,这两种家庭压力源都与父母在人际和人际层面上的负面情绪有关。人内关联仅是同时发生的,没有证据表明未来会产生预期影响。跨层次的互动表明,一生中性别认同的微攻击性暴露减弱了对父母间冲突的情绪反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,日常家庭压力过程可以作为干预目标,以支持跨性别和非二元父母家庭在公共卫生危机期间的福祉。这项研究提出了一个关于基于身份的耻辱如何与家庭压力源相互作用以影响情绪的新颖视角。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为有针对性的干预措施提供信息,以在突发公共卫生事件期间支持跨性别和非二元父母的心理健康,特别是通过解决与性别认同相关的压力源对日常情绪的影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖自我报告的数据和相对较小的样本量而受到限制。证据是中等的,因为研究结果是基于单一时间段的,可能无法推广到所有跨性别和非二元父母。

title: Risk factors for post-COVID-19 condition among previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Post-COVID-19 condition is a major source of long-term morbidity after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Patients hospitalized for COVID-19 may be at particularly high risk because hospitalization often reflects greater acute disease severity and comorbidity burden. However, evidence on risk factors in previously hospitalized populations remains inconsistent due to differences in outcome definitions, follow-up periods, and analytical approaches. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify risk factors associated with post-COVID outcomes among patients previously hospitalized for COVID-19. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA 2020 principles. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the WHO COVID-19 Global Literature Database were searched for studies published between 1 January 2020 and 24 February 2026. Eligible studies included hospitalized patients with confirmed or probable COVID-19, assessed post-acute outcomes at least 4 weeks after acute infection, hospitalization, recovery, or discharge, and evaluated at least one candidate risk factor. Adjusted effect estimates were prioritized, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed when at least two comparable estimates were available. Results Eleven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, and seven contributed to quantitative meta-analysis. Five risk-factor groups were pooled: female sex, acute disease severity or respiratory support, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, vaccination status, and hypertension. Female sex was associated with higher odds of post-COVID outcomes (OR 1.94, 95% CI 1.60–2.35; I 2 = 6.9%). The strongest association was observed for greater acute disease severity or advanced respiratory support (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.77–3.68; I 2 = 13.0%). ICU admission (OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.24–2.83), no or incomplete vaccination (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.33–2.72), and hypertension (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.16–2.20) were also associated with increased odds. Additional predictors, including obesity, age, smoking, dysgeusia, symptom burden, and neurological or psychiatric comorbidity, were summarized narratively. Conclusion Among previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients, the most consistent risk factors for post-COVID outcomes were female sex, greater acute disease severity or respiratory support, ICU admission, no or incomplete vaccination, and hypertension. These findings support risk-based post-discharge follow-up, although the evidence remains limited by heterogeneous outcome definitions and the small number of studies available for several risk factors.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review aimed to identify risk factors associated with post-COVID outcomes among patients previously hospitalized for COVID-19. The central question focused on determining which factors are most consistently linked to post-COVID-19 condition, particularly in the context of long-term morbidity following SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA 2020 principles. Eligible studies included hospitalized patients with confirmed or probable COVID-19, assessed post-acute outcomes at least 4 weeks after acute infection, hospitalization, recovery, or discharge, and evaluated at least one candidate risk factor. Adjusted effect estimates were prioritized, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed when at least two comparable estimates were available.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among previously hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection, the most consistent risk factors for post-COVID outcomes were female sex, greater acute disease severity or respiratory support, ICU admission, no or incomplete vaccination, and hypertension. These findings were supported by pooled estimates from multiple studies, with female sex showing an odds ratio of 1.94 (95% CI 1.60–2.35) and greater acute disease severity or respiratory support showing an odds ratio of 2.55 (95% CI 1.77–3.68).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence on risk factors in previously hospitalized populations remains inconsistent due to differences in outcome definitions, follow-up periods, and analytical approaches. The review also noted that additional predictors, including obesity, age, smoking, dysgeusia, symptom burden, and neurological or psychiatric comorbidity, were summarized narratively, indicating a lack of sufficient quantitative data for these factors.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings support risk-based post-discharge follow-up for previously hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. However, the evidence remains limited by heterogeneous outcome definitions and the small number of studies available for several risk factors. There is a need for further research to standardize outcome definitions and improve the understanding of less well-characterized risk factors.

title_zh: Risk factors for post-COVID-19 condition among previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
source_body_en: Background Post-COVID-19 condition is a major source of long-term morbidity after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Patients hospitalized for COVID-19 may be at particularly high risk because hospitalization often reflects greater acute disease severity and comorbidity burden. However, evidence on risk factors in previously hospitalized populations remains inconsistent due to differences in outcome definitions, follow-up periods, and analytical approaches. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify risk factors associated with post-COVID outcomes among patients previously hospitalized for COVID-19. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA 2020 principles. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and the WHO COVID-19 Global Literature Database were searched for studies published between 1 January 2020 and 24 February 2026. Eligible studies included hospitalized patients with confirmed or probable COVID-19, assessed post-acute outcomes at least 4 weeks after acute infection, hospitalization, recovery, or discharge, and evaluated at least one candidate risk factor. Adjusted effect estimates were prioritized, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed when at least two comparable estimates were available. Results Eleven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, and seven contributed to quantitative meta-analysis. Five risk-factor groups were pooled: female sex, acute disease severity or respiratory support, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, vaccination status, and hypertension. Female sex was associated with higher odds of post-COVID outcomes (OR 1.94, 95% CI 1.60–2.35; I 2 = 6.9%). The strongest association was observed for greater acute disease severity or advanced respiratory support (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.77–3.68; I 2 = 13.0%). ICU admission (OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.24–2.83), no or incomplete vaccination (OR 1.90, 95% CI 1.33–2.72), and hypertension (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.16–2.20) were also associated with increased odds. Additional predictors, including obesity, age, smoking, dysgeusia, symptom burden, and neurological or psychiatric comorbidity, were summarized narratively. Conclusion Among previously hospitalized COVID-19 patients, the most consistent risk factors for post-COVID outcomes were female sex, greater acute disease severity or respiratory support, ICU admission, no or incomplete vaccination, and hypertension. These findings support risk-based post-discharge follow-up, although the evidence remains limited by heterogeneous outcome definitions and the small number of studies available for several risk factors.

title: Genome-wide machine learning analysis of anosmia and ageusia with COVID-19.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused substantial worldwide disruptions in health, economy, and society, manifesting symptoms such as loss of smell (anosmia) and loss of taste (ageusia), that can result in prolonged sensory impairment. Establishing the host genetic etiology of anosmia and ageusia in COVID-19 will aid in the overall understanding of the sensorineural aspect of the disease and contribute to possible treatments or cures. By using human genome sequencing data from the University of Iowa (UI) COVID-19 cohort (N = 187) and the National Institute of Health All of Us (AoU) Research Program COVID-19 cohort (N = 947), we investigated the genetics of anosmia and/or ageusia by employing feature selection techniques to construct a novel variant and gene prioritization pipeline, utilizing machine learning methods for the classification of patients. Models were assessed using a permutation-based variable importance (PVI) strategy for final prioritization of candidate variants and genes. The highest held-out test set area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve for models and datasets from the UI cohort was 0.735 and 0.798 for the variant and gene analysis respectively and for the AoU cohort was 0.687 for the variant analysis. Our analysis prioritized several novel and known candidate host genetic factors involved in immune response, neuronal signaling, and calcium signaling supporting previously proposed hypotheses for anosmia/ageusia in COVID-19.

title: Comparative systemic pathogenicity and host tropism of ancestral SARS-CoV-2, Delta, and Omicron EG.5 variants in K18-hACE2 mice
abstract: Introduction SARS-CoV-2 undergoes persistent genomic evolution, yet prevalent circulating variants tend to evolve toward reduced pathogenicity. However, direct comparative pathogenesis data involving contemporary, immune-evasive strains—such as the Omicron EG.5 subvariant (a descendant of the globally dominant XBB lineage)—relative to ancestral strains remain scarce. Methods To clarify the evolutionary trajectory of viral virulence, we conducted a systematic, head-to-head comparison of the in vivo pathogenicity of three pivotal strains: the ancestral Wild-type (Wuhan lineage), Delta, and the currently circulating Omicron EG.5. We utilized the highly susceptible K18-hACE2 transgenic mouse model to assess disease progression, viral burden, and histopathology. Results Despite uniformly progressing to lethality in this model, the strains exhibited a distinct gradient in the kinetics and severity of disease. The Wild-type strain demonstrated the most rapid disease progression, highest viral loads across multiple organs (notably liver, brain, lung, and intestine), and most severe histopathological damage. The Delta variant showed an intermediate phenotype. Strikingly, the Omicron EG.5 variant displayed significantly attenuated pathogenicity, characterized by markedly delayed mortality, milder clinical presentation, and reduced tissue viral burden, yet it retained a capacity for multi-organ infection. Discussion Our study provides direct experimental evidence for a pronounced attenuation in pathogenicity along the evolutionary trajectory from Wild-type through Delta to Omicron EG.5. source_records.abstract: Introduction SARS-CoV-2 undergoes persistent genomic evolution, yet prevalent circulating variants tend to evolve toward reduced pathogenicity. However, direct comparative pathogenesis data involving contemporary, immune-evasive strains—such as the Omicron EG.5 subvariant (a descendant of the globally dominant XBB lineage)—relative to ancestral strains remain scarce. Methods To clarify the evolutionary trajectory of viral virulence, we conducted a systematic, head-to-head comparison of the in vivo pathogenicity of three pivotal strains: the ancestral Wild-type (Wuhan lineage), Delta, and the currently circulating Omicron EG.5. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the comparative systemic pathogenicity and host tropism of ancestral SARS-CoV-2, Delta, and Omicron EG.5 variants in K18-hACE2 mice. The research addresses the need for understanding how viral evolution impacts disease severity, as immune-evasive strains like EG.5 have limited direct pathogenesis data. Using a highly susceptible mouse model, the study systematically compares the in vivo effects of these variants. Results show a gradient in disease progression and severity, with the ancestral strain causing the most rapid and severe outcomes. The Omicron EG.5 variant exhibits significantly reduced pathogenicity, yet retains multi-organ infectivity. These findings offer direct experimental evidence of attenuation in pathogenicity across variants and have implications for risk assessment and surveillance of emerging strains. The study's use of an animal model limits its direct applicability to human disease, but the evidence is robust due to the clear comparative analysis.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在填补关于 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异株比较致病性的知识空白,因基因组 进化 已导致免疫逃逸株,但其对疾病严重程度的影响尚不明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染高度敏感的 K18-hACE2 转基因小鼠中,对三种关键菌株(祖先野生型(武汉谱系)、Delta 和 Omicron EG.5)的体内致病性进行了头对头比较。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用 K18-hACE2 小鼠模型来评估三种毒株的疾病进展、病毒负荷和组织病理学,从而对其致病潜力进行系统评估。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有菌株在小鼠模型中均进展至致死,但它们在疾病动力学和严重程度方面表现出明显的梯度,其中野生型菌株表现出最快的进展、最高的病毒载量和最严重的组织病理学损伤。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,从祖先菌株到 Delta 到 Omicron EG.5,致病性明显减弱,为这种进化趋势提供了直接的实验证据。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为新兴变异的风险评估提供了重要的见解,并强调了正在进行的 监测 对监测致病性变化的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于动物模型,可能无法完全反映人类疾病动态,但由于对相关 宿主 系统中关键变异的直接比较,证据是强有力的。

abstract_zh: 引言 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 经历持续的基因组 进化,但流行的流通变异株往往朝着致病性降低的方向进化。然而,涉及当代免疫逃逸株(如 Omicron EG.5 亚变异株,其为全球主导 XBB 谱系的后裔)与祖先株之间的直接比较 发病机制 数据仍然匮乏。方法 为阐明病毒毒力的进化轨迹,我们对三株关键病毒株进行了系统的头对头比较:祖先株(武汉谱系)、Delta 变异株以及当前流通的 Omicron EG.5。我们采用高易感 K18-hACE2 转基因小鼠模型评估疾病进展、病毒载量及组织病理学。结果 尽管在该模型中所有毒株均最终导致致死性结局,但其在疾病动力学和严重程度方面呈现出明显梯度差异。祖先株显示出最快的疾病进展、多器官(尤其是肝脏、脑、肺和肠道)中最高的病毒载量以及最严重的组织病理学损伤。Delta 变异株表现出中等表型。值得注意的是,Omicron EG.5 变异株的致病性显著减弱,其特征为显著延迟的 死亡率、较轻的临床表现以及降低的组织病毒载量,但仍保留多器官感染能力。讨论 本研究为从祖先株经由 Delta 至 Omicron EG.5 的进化轨迹中致病性显著减弱提供了直接实验证据。这些发现为新兴变异株的风险评估提供了关键见解,并强调了持续 监测 的必要性。

title: High rates of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection in residents of long term care facilities despite robust spike-specific immunity following serial vaccination.
abstract: Older adult residents of long-term care facilities (LTCFs) suffered high rates of mortality during the initial stages of the COVID-19 pandemic but their clinical risk has decreased markedly following vaccination. Here we determined humoral and cellular immunity following delivery of a 5th vaccine dose, an mRNA spike B1:BA.1 bivalent vaccine, to care home residents. The delivery of a 5th vaccine elicited a plateau of spike-specific immunity that remained broadly stable over 100 days in almost all people. Despite this, 15% of residents had a primary infection and 30% became reinfected during 6-months of follow up. These findings reveal that serial vaccine delivery can establish robust systemic spike-specific immune responses in frail older people but that this does not reliably prevent SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. As such, additional approaches should be considered to reduce reinfection risk in this vulnerable population group.

Here we determined humoral and cellular immunity following delivery of a 5th vaccine dose, an mRNA spike B1:BA.1 bivalent vaccine, to care home residents. The delivery of a 5th vaccine elicited a plateau of spike-specific immunity that remained broadly stable over 100 days in almost all people. Despite this, 15% of residents had a primary infection and 30% became reinfected during 6-months of follow up. These findings reveal that serial vaccine delivery can establish robust systemic spike-specific immune responses in frail older people but that this does not reliably prevent SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. As such, additional approaches should be considered to reduce reinfection risk in this vulnerable population group.

title: Immunothrombotic Features of Coronary Thrombi in Myocardial Infarction after SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination
abstract: Summary Background Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute to immunothrombosis and arterial thrombosis. Mechanisms underlying myocardial infarction after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination remain poorly understood. Objectives To investigate histopathologic and immunothrombotic features of coronary thrombi in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. Methods We performed a retrospective matched cohort study including patients with STEMI undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention between January 2021 and March 2023. Coronary thrombi obtained by aspiration were analyzed by histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and confocal microscopy for NET detection. Vaccinated and unvaccinated patients were matched by age and sex. Associations between vaccination status and thrombus characteristics were assessed after adjustment for SARS-CoV-2 serologic status. Results Among 44 matched patients (23 vaccinated and 21 unvaccinated), NETs were identified in 14 vaccinated patients (61%) and 5 unvaccinated patients (24%; P = .01). Vaccination was associated with increased odds of NET-positive thrombi after adjustment for SARS-CoV-2 serology (odds ratio, 5.1; 95% CI, 1.36–19.45; P = .02). No associations were observed between vaccination and polymorphonuclear cell density, fibrin deposits, plaque fragments, or anti–platelet factor 4 staining. Among patients vaccinated within 100 days before STEMI, NET-positive thrombi were associated with shorter intervals between vaccination and myocardial infarction (median [IQR], 25 [11–64] vs 57 [40–84] days; P = .02). Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 vaccination was associated with increased NET presence in coronary thrombi from patients with STEMI, suggesting a potential NET-mediated immunothrombotic mechanism independent of classical vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia.

title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 心肌梗死后冠状动脉血栓的免疫血栓特征
source_body_en: Summary Background Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contribute to immunothrombosis and arterial thrombosis. Mechanisms underlying myocardial infarction after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination remain poorly understood. Objectives To investigate histopathologic and immunothrombotic features of coronary thrombi in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. Methods We performed a retrospective matched cohort study including patients with STEMI undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention between January 2021 and March 2023. Coronary thrombi obtained by aspiration were analyzed by histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and confocal microscopy for NET detection. Vaccinated and unvaccinated patients were matched by age and sex. Associations between vaccination status and thrombus characteristics were assessed after adjustment for SARS-CoV-2 serologic status. Results Among 44 matched patients (23 vaccinated and 21 unvaccinated), NETs were identified in 14 vaccinated patients (61%) and 5 unvaccinated patients (24%; P = .01). Vaccination was associated with increased odds of NET-positive thrombi after adjustment for SARS-CoV-2 serology (odds ratio, 5.1; 95% CI, 1.36–19.45; P = .02). No associations were observed between vaccination and polymorphonuclear cell density, fibrin deposits, plaque fragments, or anti–platelet factor 4 staining. Among patients vaccinated within 100 days before STEMI, NET-positive thrombi were associated with shorter intervals between vaccination and myocardial infarction (median [IQR], 25 [11–64] vs 57 [40–84] days; P = .02). Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 vaccination was associated with increased NET presence in coronary thrombi from patients with STEMI, suggesting a potential NET-mediated immunothrombotic mechanism independent of classical vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Viral Respiratory Testing in Children With Abnormal Urinalysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Respiratory viral panels (RVP) are common, expensive tests that often do not change treatment, especially in children with suspected urinary tract infections. In children with abnormal urinalysis (UA) results, we hypothesize that RVP overuse existed before the COVID-19 pandemic and has risen further after. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of children aged 0 to 24 months who presented to a quaternary care children's emergency department (ED) from March 2018 to May 2025 with abnormal UA results. Children with complex chronic conditions, required intensive care or respiratory support, or sepsis were excluded. The primary outcome was the proportion of children with RVP testing within periods of prepandemic (March 2018-February 2020), pandemic (March 2020-May 2023), and postpandemic (July 2023-May 2025). Secondary outcomes included ED revisits, antiviral use, and cost of testing. We assessed trends in RVP use across the periods using interrupted time series analysis. Cost was measured using Medicaid reimbursement fees. RESULTS: Our cohort included 7496 patients. The proportion of all children who received an RVP was 25.0% (95% CI, 23.1-27.0), 68.1% (95% CI, 66.5-69.7), and 66.1% (95% CI, 64.1-68.0) during prepandemic, pandemic, and postpandemic periods, respectively. There was an increase in viral testing during the pandemic compared with prepandemic period (P < .001) but without change between pandemic and postpandemic (P = .14). Viral testing was associated with no differences in ED revisits (P = .41). Only 134 patients (1.8%) received antivirals. The total cost of respiratory viral testing was $1 037 978. CONCLUSIONS: RVP testing increased during the COVID-19 pandemic in children with abnormal UA results and remained elevated postpandemic. RVP testing was costly and associated with low antiviral use. These results highlight opportunities for diagnostic stewardship.

elements_zh.main_results: 在大流行前时期,接受呼吸道病毒检测(RVP)的儿童比例为25.0%(95%置信区间,23.1-27.0);在大流行期间为68.1%(95%置信区间,66.5-69.7);在大流行后时期为66.1%(95%置信区间,64.1-68.0)。与大流行前时期相比,大流行期间的比例显著上升(P < .001),但在大流行与大流行后期间无显著变化(P = .14)。仅134名患者(1.8%)接受了抗病毒药物,呼吸道病毒检测的总成本为1 037 978美元。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,在大流行期间,尿液分析结果异常的儿童的 RVP 检测有所增加,并且在大流行后仍保持较高水平,这凸显了在这种情况下进行诊断管理的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,在大流行期间对尿液分析结果异常的儿童过度使用 RVP 检测可能会导致不必要的医疗费用,而对急诊复诊等临床结果的影响有限。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其单中心设计和回顾性而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。由于缺乏随机性和潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether the use of respiratory viral panels (RVP) in children with abnormal urinalysis results increased during the COVID-19 pandemic compared to the prepandemic period, as RVPs are common, expensive tests that often do not alter treatment in such cases.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted at a quaternary care children's emergency department, involving children aged 0 to 24 months with abnormal urinalysis results from March 2018 to May 2025. Patients with complex chronic conditions, requiring intensive care or respiratory support, or sepsis were excluded.
analysis_en.methods: The study used interrupted time series analysis to assess trends in RVP use across the prepandemic, pandemic, and postpandemic periods. The primary outcome was the proportion of children receiving RVP testing, while secondary outcomes included ED revisits, antiviral use, and cost of testing, measured using Medicaid reimbursement fees.
analysis_en.main_results: The proportion of children receiving RVP testing was 25.0% (95% CI, 23.1-27.0) during the prepandemic period, 68.1% (95% CI, 66.5-69.7) during the pandemic, and 66.1% (95% CI, 64.1-68.0) in the postpandemic period. There was a significant increase during the pandemic compared to the prepandemic period (P < .001), but no change between pandemic and postpandemic (P = .14). Only 134 patients (1.8%) received antivirals, and the total cost of respiratory viral testing was $1 037 978.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that RVP testing increased during the pandemic in children with abnormal urinalysis results and remained elevated postpandemic, highlighting the need for diagnostic stewardship in this context.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the overuse of RVP testing in children with abnormal urinalysis results during the pandemic may have contributed to unnecessary healthcare costs, with limited impact on clinical outcomes such as ED revisits.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-center design and retrospective nature, which may affect generalisability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the lack of randomisation and potential for confounding factors.

title_zh: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Viral Respiratory Testing in Children With Abnormal Urinalysis.
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: Respiratory viral panels (RVP) are common, expensive tests that often do not change treatment, especially in children with suspected urinary tract infections. In children with abnormal urinalysis (UA) results, we hypothesize that RVP overuse existed before the COVID-19 pandemic and has risen further after. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of children aged 0 to 24 months who presented to a quaternary care children's emergency department (ED) from March 2018 to May 2025 with abnormal UA results. Children with complex chronic conditions, required intensive care or respiratory support, or sepsis were excluded. The primary outcome was the proportion of children with RVP testing within periods of prepandemic (March 2018-February 2020), pandemic (March 2020-May 2023), and postpandemic (July 2023-May 2025). Secondary outcomes included ED revisits, antiviral use, and cost of testing. We assessed trends in RVP use across the periods using interrupted time series analysis. Cost was measured using Medicaid reimbursement fees. RESULTS: Our cohort included 7496 patients. The proportion of all children who received an RVP was 25.0% (95% CI, 23.1-27.0), 68.1% (95% CI, 66.5-69.7), and 66.1% (95% CI, 64.1-68.0) during prepandemic, pandemic, and postpandemic periods, respectively. There was an increase in viral testing during the pandemic compared with prepandemic period (P < .001) but without change between pandemic and postpandemic (P = .14). Viral testing was associated with no differences in ED revisits (P = .41). Only 134 patients (1.8%) received antivirals. The total cost of respiratory viral testing was $1 037 978. CONCLUSIONS: RVP testing increased during the COVID-19 pandemic in children with abnormal UA results and remained elevated postpandemic. RVP testing was costly and associated with low antiviral use. These results highlight opportunities for diagnostic stewardship.

title: Potent type-specific de novo antibodies complement broadly reactive imprinted antibodies in immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 variants.
abstract: For rapidly mutating viruses such as influenza viruses and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), immune memory recalled by antigenically drifted variants primarily comprises antibodies that cross-react to the priming strain rather than de novo elicited responses, a phenomenon termed original antigenic sin or immune imprinting. The composition and functionality of de novo responses elicited by variant exposures remain unclear. Here we isolated and characterized hundreds of recall and de novo neutralizing monoclonal antibodies after sequential exposures to SARS-CoV-2 variants in ancestral-imprinted humans. De novo variant type-specific antibodies used different V(D)J genes that were closer to germline sequence, potently neutralized future variants and targeted distinct receptor binding domain epitopes compared to ancestral cross-reactive (recall) antibodies. Nevertheless, neutralizing responses to the updated 2024-2025 booster were predominantly ancestral cross-reactive. These results reveal the distinct contributions of recall and de novo antibodies to a balanced immune response and underscore the benefit of updated booster vaccines, which augment both subsets.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding the composition and functionality of de novo responses elicited by variant exposures, particularly in the context of rapidly mutating viruses like SARS-CoV-2 where immune memory is dominated by cross-reactive antibodies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved isolating and characterizing hundreds of recall and de novo neutralizing monoclonal antibodies from ancestral-imprinted humans after sequential exposures to SARS-CoV-2 variants, conducted between 2024 and 2025.
analysis.methods: The researchers used sequential exposures to SARS-CoV-2 variants to isolate and characterize neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, focusing on their V(D)J gene usage, neutralization potency, and epitope targeting.
analysis.main_results: De novo variant type-specific antibodies utilized V(D)J genes closer to germline sequences, potently neutralized future variants, and targeted distinct receptor binding domain epitopes compared to ancestral cross-reactive antibodies.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that de novo antibodies provide distinct neutralizing capabilities against SARS-CoV-2 variants, highlighting the importance of updated booster vaccines in enhancing immune responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the development of updated booster vaccines that can augment both recall and de novo antibody subsets, contributing to more effective immunity against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on monoclonal antibody characterization, which may not fully represent the complexity of natural immune responses. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 variants by isolating and characterizing de novo and recall neutralizing monoclonal antibodies. It reveals that de novo antibodies, elicited by variant exposures, target distinct epitopes and use V(D)J genes closer to germline sequences compared to ancestral cross-reactive antibodies. Despite their potency, neutralizing responses to the 2024-2025 booster were predominantly ancestral cross-reactive, underscoring the need for updated vaccines to enhance both antibody subsets. The findings contribute to understanding the balance between recall and de novo responses and support the use of updated booster vaccines for improved immunity against emerging variants. The study is based on abstract-only evidence, and while the results are informative, the evidence strength is moderate due to the limited scope of monoclonal antibody analysis.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在 2024 年至 2025 年间进行,对来自祖先印记人类连续暴露于 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体后的数百种回忆和从头中和单克隆抗体进行了分离和表征。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的连续暴露来分离和表征中和单克隆抗体,重点关注其 V(D)J 基因使用、中和效力和表位靶向。
elements_zh.main_results: 与祖先交叉反应抗体相比,从头变体类型特异性抗体利用更接近种系序列的 V(D)J 基因,有效中和未来变体,并靶向不同的受体结合域表位。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,从头抗体对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体提供了独特的中和能力,突出了更新的加强剂 疫苗 在增强 免疫应答 方面的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为更新增强剂 疫苗 的开发提供了信息,该增强剂可以增强召回和从头抗体子集,从而有助于更有效地抵抗新兴的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象证据,结果基于单克隆抗体表征,可能无法完全代表天然 免疫应答 的复杂性。证据强度中等。
